title: Ordered tensor composition on shifted regular units
statement:
Let $\mathcal X$ be a small site and $R$ a sheaf of commutative rings in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Use ordinary sheaves of $R$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], their unbounded derived category $D(R)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and the K-flat derived tensor with its usual unitors and signed cochain symmetry [lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal]. Put $I=R[0]$, $S_n=I[-n]$ for $n\in\mathbf Z$, and $m:I\otimes_R^LI\to I$ equal to unit multiplication. Use the signed tensor/shift comparisons of [lem-weil-pbc-derived-tensor-shift-descent]: first-shift extraction is unsigned and second-shift extraction by $b$ multiplies a summand with first-factor degree $a$ by $(-1)^{ab}$. Let $r_{p,q}:S_{p+q}\xrightarrow{\sim}S_p\otimes_R^LS_q$ be the inverse of the comparison obtained by extracting first the first shift, then the second, followed by $m[-p-q]$, with ordinary addition of shifts.

Define $\kappa_{Z,q}:Z\otimes_R^LS_q\xrightarrow{\sim}Z[-q]$ to be extraction of the second shift $-q$ followed by the shifted right unitor. For every derived object $Z$ it is natural in $Z$, on arbitrary derived morphisms. One has $\kappa_{I,q}=\lambda_{S_q}$, with $\lambda$ the left unitor. For all integers $p,q$ and arbitrary derived arrows $f:S_p\to I$, $g:S_q\to I$, the following is an equality of maps $S_p\otimes_R^LS_q\to I$:
$$m(f\otimes g)=g\lambda_{S_q}(f\otimes1)=g\kappa_{I,q}(f\otimes1)=g f[-q]\kappa_{S_p,q}.$$
There is a function $t:\mathbf Z\times\mathbf Z\to\{1,-1\}$ fixed solely by these integer shift/extraction conventions, uniformly for all small sites and all $R$, such that
$$\kappa_{S_p,q}r_{p,q}=t_{p,q}\operatorname{can}_{p,q},\qquad t_{p,0}=t_{0,q}=1,$$
where $\operatorname{can}_{p,q}:S_{p+q}\xrightarrow{\sim}S_p[-q]$ is ordinary shift addition. Consequently
$$m(f\otimes g)r_{p,q}=t_{p,q}\,g f[-q]\operatorname{can}_{p,q}.$$
The function $t$ is independent of $R$, the site and the arrows, including when $R=0$. The equalities concern morphisms in the derived category; neither $f$ nor $g$ is required to admit a chain-map representative between the displayed unit complexes.

proof.text: We may compute the structural maps on the displayed unit complexes. By [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed], tensoring a module sheaf with $R$ is naturally the identity, so $R$ is flat by [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. Each $I[-n]$ is bounded with flat terms and hence K-flat by [lem-pc-kflat-closure]. Using the definition [def-pc-kflat-complex] and the shift functor [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], the same argument shows that shifting a flat-term K-flat complex preserves this property: it preserves flat terms, and tensoring an acyclic complex with the shift is a shift of the original acyclic tensor, by [lem-weil-pbc-total-tensor-integer-shifts]. Thus the stability assumption in [lem-weil-pbc-derived-tensor-shift-descent] holds. Its representative comparisons and those of [lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal] identify the structural maps used below with their total-complex formulas. This computation chooses representatives only for structural maps, never for the arrows $f,g$.

proof.text: Write $t^2_{-q}$ for second-shift extraction. By [lem-weil-pbc-derived-tensor-shift-descent] it is an isomorphism natural in the first variable on every derived arrow. The right unitor is a natural isomorphism by [lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal] and [def-sfb-monoidal-category]. Hence $\kappa_{Z,q}=\rho_Z[-q]\,t^2_{-q}(Z,I)$ is a natural isomorphism, and for every $h:Z\to Z'$ its naturality equation is $\kappa_{Z',q}(h\otimes1)=h[-q]\kappa_{Z,q}$. This uses naturality in $D(R)$ itself, including inverses of quasi-isomorphisms.

source.place: Paragraph (3), internal bar normalization supplied by agent; proof step 2. Sign convention: Stacks Tag 0FNH, item-shift-tensor; no claim that the blueprint spells out this auxiliary argument.

proof.text: For $Z=I$, the only first-factor degree is $0$, so second-shift extraction has coefficient $(-1)^{(-q)0}=1$ by [lem-weil-pbc-total-tensor-integer-shifts]. On the sole nonzero summand $R\otimes_RR$ both $\rho_I[-q]t^2_{-q}(I,I)$ and $\lambda_{S_q}$ are multiplication $a\otimes b\mapsto ab$. The structural representative identifications of step 1 therefore give $\kappa_{I,q}=\lambda_{S_q}$ in $D(R)$. The same multiplication formula gives $m=\lambda_I=\rho_I$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), internal bar normalization supplied by agent; proof step 3. Sign convention: Stacks Tag 0FNH, item-shift-tensor; no claim that the blueprint spells out this auxiliary argument.

proof.text: Tensor bifunctoriality gives $f\otimes g=(1_I\otimes g)(f\otimes1_{S_q})$. Naturality of the left unitor at the derived arrow $g:S_q\to I$ gives $m(1_I\otimes g)=g\lambda_{S_q}$, since $m=\lambda_I$. Using step 3 and then step 2 with $h=f$ yields precisely $m(f\otimes g)=g\lambda_{S_q}(f\otimes1)=g\kappa_{I,q}(f\otimes1)=g f[-q]\kappa_{S_p,q}$. These are typed equalities from $S_p\otimes_R^LS_q$ to $I$; no realization of $f$ or $g$ by a chain map was used.

source.place: Paragraph (3), internal bar normalization supplied by agent; proof step 4. Sign convention: Stacks Tag 0FNH, item-shift-tensor; no claim that the blueprint spells out this auxiliary argument.

proof.text: Compute $r_{p,q}$ and $\kappa_{S_p,q}$ on the unit complexes using step 1. In the comparison whose inverse is $r_{p,q}$, extracting the first shift $-p$ is unsigned. After this extraction the first factor is the unshifted $I$, so extracting the second shift $-q$ is also unsigned. Thus this comparison is the multiplication isomorphism $R\otimes_RR\to R$ on the unique summand in degree $p+q$, with no scalar sign. Its inverse sends a local section $a$ to $a\otimes1$. In contrast, the extraction in $\kappa_{S_p,q}$ has first-factor degree $p$, so its coefficient is $(-1)^{(-q)p}=(-1)^{pq}$. Its remaining right unitor is multiplication. Consequently $\kappa_{S_p,q}r_{p,q}=(-1)^{pq}\operatorname{can}_{p,q}$ as maps in $D(R)$, since ordinary shift addition is unsigned on these complexes. The local formulas determine maps of sheaves (simple tensors generate the tensor presheaf, and its sheafification defines the sheaf tensor).

source.place: Paragraph (3), internal bar normalization supplied by agent; proof step 5. Sign convention: Stacks Tag 0FNH, item-shift-tensor; no claim that the blueprint spells out this auxiliary argument.

proof.text: Define $t_{p,q}$ to be $1$ when $pq$ is even and $-1$ when $pq$ is odd. This is a function of the integers alone, before choosing a site or a ring; it equals the coefficient in step 5 and gives $t_{p,0}=t_{0,q}=1$. Precompose the equality of step 4 by $r_{p,q}$ and substitute step 5 to obtain the final formula. All formulas also hold for the zero ring, where every displayed map is the unique map between zero objects. We have not attempted to recover $t_{p,q}$ from those maps, so this degenerate case causes no ambiguity in the uniformly defined function.
